item.title: Ethics and Entrepreneurship: Foundations and Philosophical Perspectives
item.content:encoded:
Tina Dacin, Wilfrid Laurier University

Robin Holt, University of Bristol

Jean Clarke, Emlyon Business School

Jaco Lok, Macquarie University

Max Ganzin, Macquarie University

This special issue examines the ethical foundations of entrepreneurship, positioning ethics as central to entrepreneurial practice rather than a constraint on it. The issue brings together entrepreneurship studies and philosophical ethics to explore how venture creation, opportunity recognition, and stakeholder engagement involve fundamental questions about responsibility, justice, and human flourishing. It investigates the tension between entrepreneurship's capacity for creativity and disruption and concerns about commodification and self-optimization.

The special issue welcomes diverse methodological and disciplinary perspectives examining how philosophical traditions such as virtue ethics, phenomenology, pragmatism, and deontology illuminate entrepreneurial practice. It particularly emphasizes entrepreneurial decision-making under uncertainty and fluidity, where ethical judgment must balance competing stakeholder interests without reliance on established protocols. The issue seeks papers exploring how entrepreneurship and ethics can deepen each other's understanding through examining contingency, creativity, authenticity, care, and emerging futures.

Appel publié par Journal of Business Ethics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Philosophical dimensions of ethics and how different philosophical traditions inform understanding of entrepreneurship as an ethical practice
  • Phenomenology of the entrepreneurial experience, uncertainty, autonomy, and decision-making
  • The entrepreneur and ethical subjectivity, agency, embodiment, and identity
  • Ethics and rule-breaking in entrepreneurial contexts
  • Stakeholder relations, trust-building, and ethical objectives
  • Whether entrepreneurship is inherently ethical or exploitative
  • Entrepreneurship and technological mediation in the digital age
  • Ethics, value, and the framing of entrepreneurial goals and opportunities
  • Temporal dimensions of entrepreneurial ethics and long-term considerations

Timeline

  • September 30, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: The Ethics of Gender Paradoxes in Organizations
item.content:encoded:
Pauline Reinecke, Leuphana University Lüneburg

Ignas Bruder, Technische Universität Dresden

Tobias Hahn, Esade Business School

Olga Kokshagina, University of Sydney

Stephanie Schrage, Kiel University

Janina Sundermeier, Freie Universität Berlin

Gender paradoxes emerge from tensions embedded in organizations, where competing expectations generate not only managerial challenges but also fundamental ethical questions about inclusion, equality, and responsibility. While prior research has examined barriers such as the glass ceiling and pay inequality, less attention has been paid to how gender paradoxes subtly yet systematically shape organizational experiences and allocate moral responsibilities among actors.

Gender is approached as an institutionalized system of social practices for constituting people as two significantly different categories, men and women, and organizing social relations of inequality on the basis of that difference. At the same time, the special issue recognizes the lived realities of intersex, non-binary, genderfluid, and other gender-diverse individuals who navigate structures grounded in binary norms.

Appel publié par Journal of Business Ethics. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Systemic constraints: How ethical commitments to inclusion and equality clash with organizational systems optimized for efficiency – such as standardized evaluations, established management practices, or masculinized leadership norms
  • Competing values and moral ambiguity: How ideals such as fairness, meritocracy, and equity create ethical tensions and "tragic choices", where no option is without compromise
  • Limits of both/and thinking: How both/and strategies for navigating gender paradoxes can foster more inclusive responses, but may also obscure structural inequalities and shift responsibility to individuals
  • Symbolic inclusion and tokenism: How efforts such as diversity targets or flexible work arrangements may produce ethically problematic outcomes, including constrained agency, limited advancement, and superficial change
  • Stigma, visibility, and marginalization: How gender-diverse professionals experience and resist stigmatization within organizations, raising ethical questions about who bears the burden of representation

Timeline

  • August 31, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: Responsible and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence in Tourism and Hospitality
item.content:encoded:
Brian King, Texas A&M University

Kyoung Jun Lee, Kyung Hee University

Danae Manika, Brunel University of London

Babak Taheri, Texas A&M University

This special issue seeks to advance understanding of how artificial intelligence can be designed and deployed responsibly and trustworthily within tourism and hospitality sectors. As AI becomes increasingly embedded in service delivery, marketing, operations, and guest experiences, the sector faces both opportunities for innovation and significant ethical challenges regarding fairness, accountability, transparency, and consumer trust.

The special issue invites interdisciplinary research examining the technical, managerial, legal, and societal dimensions of responsible AI adoption. Submissions should explore the design, governance, and impacts of AI-enabled platforms and systems, addressing topics such as algorithmic bias, consumer trust, sustainable AI applications, ethical frameworks, digital transformation, and labor implications within tourism and hospitality contexts.

Appel publié par Electronic Markets. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Ethical AI frameworks in tourism and hospitality: fairness, accountability, transparency, and inclusivity
  • AI-driven consumer experiences: balancing personalization, convenience, and privacy
  • AI robustness and risk: testing booking, pricing, and chatbot vulnerabilities, modeling threats, and strengthening resilience
  • Trust, reliability and safety: building consumer trust, ensuring reliable performance, and managing risks
  • Auditing AI systems: ongoing evaluations in pursuit of fairness, accuracy, and compliance
  • Generative AI in marketing: pursuing responsibility in branding, engagement, and consumer journeys
  • Sociotechnical and cultural dimensions: cross-cultural and historical perspectives on AI adoption
  • AI, sustainability, and CSR: supporting or hindering responsible and sustainable practices in tourism and hospitality
  • Future directions: conceptual frameworks and policy challenges for responsible and trustworthy AI in service innovation and resilience
  • Social and labor impacts: the effects of adopting AI on employment, equity, and workforce well-being
  • Frugal AI and digital twins: cost-effective and resource-conscious applications for operations and guest experiences
  • Algorithmic transparency and rights: making AI decisions understandable and offering recourse for affected consumers
  • Dark side of AI: risks of manipulation, surveillance, over-automation, and addictive design
  • Corporate digital responsibility (CDR) in the age of AI within tourism and hospitality
  • AI on digital platforms: exploring recommender systems, marketplaces, and platform governance
  • Data ecosystems: sharing and leveraging user/usage data across digital travel and hospitality platforms
  • Trustworthy AI principles: ensuring AI systems in tourism and hospitality are lawful, ethical, and technically robust
  • Verification, validation, and explainability: designing AI that is interpretable and auditable for multiple stakeholders
  • Trustworthy AI and consumer journeys: balancing automation with transparency and user empowerment

Timeline

  • September 15, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: Algorithmic and behavioral biases in the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in work processes: organizational, ethical, and socio-technical implications
item.content:encoded:
Zuzana Virglerova, Tomas Bata University in Zlín

Nicola Capolupo, San Raffaele Roma University

The aim of this special issue is to explore how algorithmic and behavioral biases influence the adoption, use, and outcomes of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in organizational settings. As AI systems increasingly shape decision-making, human resource management, operational processes, and strategic planning, understanding how biases emerge and interact within socio-technical systems has become a critical scholarly and societal challenge.

The special issue seeks to integrate interdisciplinary perspectives to explain how biases arise both from AI systems and from the human and organizational decisions that design, implement, interpret, and govern them. It offers an original contribution by bridging two research streams that are often treated separately: algorithmic biases embedded in data, models, and computational architectures, and behavioral biases rooted in human cognition, organizational routines, and institutional structures. Building on socio-technical systems theory, AI is conceived as co-constructed by technologies, individuals, and the environments.

Appel publié par Business Process Management Journal. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Algorithmic biases in AI systems applied to HR and decision-making processes
  • Cognitive and behavioral biases of users interacting with AI systems
  • Governance, ethics, and regulation of AI in organizations
  • Methodologies for identifying and mitigating socio-technical biases in work processes
  • Organizational and social impacts of AI on equity, environment, inclusion, and job quality

Timeline

  • June 1, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • July 31, 2027: Closing date for manuscripts submission
